Command replay (a class of call, not one reported incident)

Write a Slack bot token into a config file: how to stop it

What happens

Write a Slack bot token into a config file. The call below tries to write a secret into a file. The agent sends it through its Write tool, and it involves Slack.

The call

{
  "file_path": "config/slack.json",
  "content": "{\"token\": \"xoxb-1234567890-abcdefghij\"}\n"
}

Tool: Write. The replay uses placeholder tokens and hosts only.

Fix it without us

Read the Slack token from an environment variable or a secret store, and do not write it into a config file. If a token reached a file, rotate it in your Slack app settings.

What KYA does

Replay result: Stopped. In the replay test, the local hook denies the call and names the rule.

Rule secret-write-slack, first stopped in version 0.33.0.

The hook is local and advisory. It fails open: if kya breaks or times out, the call goes ahead.

Install

For Claude Code, the host this replay ran on:

/plugin marketplace add The-Pixel-Boys/shield-kya
/plugin install kya@shield-kya

For any host:

npm i -g @shield-agent/kya@latest && kya start
